> 大道廢，有仁義；慧智出，有大偽；六親不和，有孝慈；國家昏亂，有忠臣.

Four sentences, four pairs of cause and effect, all built the same way. First a 廢, an 出, a 不和, a 昏亂 — then an 仁義, a 大偽, a 孝慈, a 忠臣.

The chapter is not an attack on benevolence, filial piety, or loyal ministers. Anyone who reads it that way has confused the diagnosis with the illness.

It is pointing at an order: these things appear because they were needed. And the need is the signal.

## What the sentence shape says

The grammar is the argument. Each line puts the good thing second, and derives it from a prior loss.

- 大道廢 → 有仁義: when the way is lost, benevolence and righteousness appear.
- 慧智出 → 有大偽: when cleverness is promoted, great falsity takes shape.
- 六親不和 → 有孝慈: when the family is not in accord, filial piety is praised.
- 國家昏亂 → 有忠臣: when the state is in chaos, loyal ministers stand out.

Nothing here says benevolence is bad. It says benevolence becomes a topic when the ground that made it ordinary has cracked.

## Why promotion is evidence of absence

A thing that is working does not need to be raised as a standard. We do not put up banners saying "people should breathe." We do put up banners about things that have stopped being automatic.

So when a virtue is singled out, praised, and made into a curriculum, the first question is not "how do we make people more virtuous?" but "what used to carry this, and why is it no longer carrying it?"

The 仁義 of the Confucians and Mohists, in Laozi's reading, is a repair. Repairs are necessary once the break has happened. But a repair is not the same as the original condition, and treating the repair as the goal locks in the loss.

## 大偽

The second pair is the sharpest: 慧智出，有大偽.

When cleverness becomes the currency, falsity becomes profitable. Not because clever people are dishonest, but because a system that rewards cleverness will select for the appearance of cleverness, and appearance is cheaper to produce than the thing itself.

Every metric that measures a quality creates a market in imitations of that quality. This is not cynicism; it is a mechanical consequence of measuring.

## The shape of the gap

> 凡被單獨標舉的，都是缺口的形狀.

Whatever gets held up on its own is the shape of a gap. That is the chapter's general rule, and it applies far beyond the Spring and Autumn period.

A company that suddenly runs a campaign about integrity is telling you where its processes have stopped holding. A family that has to state its values out loud has usually just lost the habit that made those values unnecessary to state.

None of this argues for cynicism about virtue. It argues for reading the banner as a diagnostic instrument rather than as a description of the state of things.

## The direction of repair

If the good thing appears as a repair, then the repair has a direction: restore the ground, not the banner.

That is what chapter 19 will do: it does not say "stop being benevolent"; it says take the signboard down and put something underneath it. 見素抱樸 — show the unworked, hold the log.
